research_gaps: No curated, up-to-date repository of large‑model monocular depth estimation papers (2023‑2025) with standardized summaries and metrics.
Absence of a comprehensive benchmark covering diverse domains (indoor, outdoor, aerial, agricultural) and real‑time constraints for evaluating large‑scale depth models.
Limited exploration of foundation‑model scaling laws, multimodal pre‑training, and uncertainty quantification specific to monocular depth estimation.
Insufficient methods for efficient adaptation (domain adaptation, few‑shot fine‑tuning) of massive depth models to new sensor setups and resource‑restricted platforms.

proposals.name: Unified Large‑Model Depth Benchmark (ULMDB)
proposals.rationale: Collect and harmonize existing datasets across multiple domains, provide standard evaluation protocols (accuracy, runtime, memory, uncertainty), and host a leaderboard for transformer‑based and diffusion‑based depth models.
proposals.expected_benefit: Enables reproducible comparison, drives community progress, and surfaces real‑world performance gaps such as latency and domain shift.
proposals.risk: High initial curation effort and potential licensing constraints on proprietary datasets.

proposals.name: Vision‑Language‑Depth Foundation Model (VLDFM)
proposals.rationale: Pre‑train a large transformer on billions of web‑scale RGB images paired with noisy depth cues derived from stereo, structure‑from‑motion, and language descriptions, using contrastive and masked depth prediction objectives.
proposals.expected_benefit: Leverages scaling laws to produce a zero‑shot depth estimator that generalizes across domains, reduces dependence on task‑specific data, and can be fine‑tuned with minimal labels.
proposals.risk: Requires massive compute and careful handling of noisy pseudo‑depth; risk of propagating systematic bias from web data.

proposals.name: Adaptive Distillation with Depth‑Sensitive Normalization (ADDSN)
proposals.rationale: Build on recent findings that global depth normalization can hurt distillation; introduce a per‑region, uncertainty‑aware normalization and a student‑teacher curriculum that focuses on hard depth ranges.
proposals.expected_benefit: Produces compact student models (~50 % parameters) that retain the accuracy of large teachers while improving robustness to pseudo‑label noise, facilitating deployment on edge devices.
proposals.risk: Complex training pipeline; may require careful hyper‑parameter tuning to avoid over‑fitting to teacher errors.
